title: CNOT-Distance is NP-complete under all-to-all connectivity
authors: Antonio Acuaviva, Arturo Acuaviva, Pablo Acuaviva
abstract: Given $A\in\operatorname{GL}(N,2)$ and an integer $K$, we ask whether $A$ can be implemented by at most $K$ CNOT gates on fixed labelled wires with all-to-all connectivity. We prove that this problem is NP-complete. From a finite simple graph $G=(V,E)$, we construct an upper-unitriangular matrix $A_G\in\operatorname{GL}(2|V|+|E|+1,2)$ satisfying $\ell_{\mathrm{CNOT}}(A_G)=2|V|+2|E|+τ(G)$, where $τ(G)$ is the minimum vertex-cover size. Each target matrix has $O(N)$ nonzero entries and row Hamming weight at most four. The lower bound unfolds an arbitrary CNOT circuit into an XOR directed acyclic graph and applies projection--contraction operations, allowing cancellation and unrestricted reuse of intermediate parities. For this family, the optimum is unchanged by any finite number of clean or borrowed ancillary wires that must be restored. A polynomial-time decoder further yields NP-hardness of approximation within every fixed additive constant and, through an L-reduction from Minimum Vertex Cover on cubic graphs, APX-hardness of the associated CNOT-circuit optimisation problem.
summary: This paper proves that calculating the minimum number of CNOT gates required to implement a given linear transformation (CNOT-Distance) is an NP-complete problem. The authors achieve this by constructing specific matrices whose gate count exactly matches the size of the minimum vertex cover of a graph. This result establishes a strong theoretical lower bound on the complexity of quantum circuit synthesis.
main_problem: The problem addressed is determining if a given invertible linear transformation $A \in GL(N, 2)$ can be implemented using at most $K$ CNOT gates ($	ext{CNOT-Distance}$).
main_result: The authors prove that the $	ext{CNOT-Distance}$ problem is NP-complete under all-to-all connectivity.
method: The proof relies on a reduction from Minimum Vertex Cover (an NP-complete problem) and involves analyzing the structure of CNOT circuits by mapping them to XOR directed acyclic graphs.
model_or_system: The model is quantum circuit synthesis using only CNOT gates acting on fixed labeled wires, represented mathematically by linear transformations over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
key_observables: $\ell_{	ext{CNOT}}(A)$ (minimum gate count), $	au(G)$ (minimum vertex cover size).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes all-to-all connectivity between any pair of distinct wires.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the NP-completeness by constructing a specific matrix $A_G$ derived from an arbitrary graph $G$, showing that $\ell_{	ext{CNOT}}(A_G)$ exactly encodes the minimum vertex cover size, thus linking circuit complexity to graph theory.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental computational hardness results for quantum circuit synthesis, which is crucial for understanding the limits of implementing desired unitary operations using physical hardware constraints.
